name: Calvin / Nameloc
title: Guardian / Protector
subtitle: Spiritbound Guardian of the Great Hound
summary: Calvin is bonded to an ancient and powerful Dog Spirit. In moments of danger, loyalty, or protection, he can unleash the spirit as Nameloc—a massive glowing guardian hound. The spirit chose him for his courage, instinct, and willingness to stand between danger and his friends.
details: Calvin is the boy form; Nameloc is the bonded Great Hound spirit form.

powers.name: Keen Nose
powers.description: Tracks creatures, people, animals, magical disturbances, and unusual spiritual scents.

powers.name: Guardian Instinct
powers.description: Can react instantly to protect an ally in danger. The original guardian rule grants one automatic success per encounter.

powers.name: Unleash the Great Hound
powers.description: Once per session, Calvin transforms into Nameloc or summons Nameloc beside him as a separate 10–15-foot glowing guardian presence.

powers.name: Titan Leap
powers.description: Leap great distances, cross gaps, save allies, break obstacles, or slam into enemies and terrain.

powers.name: Pack Protector
powers.description: Shields allies with spirit energy. Enemies may roll with disadvantage against protected allies.

powers.name: Spirit Sight
powers.description: Sees invisible enemies, hidden magic, spiritual disturbances, and threats concealed from normal vision.

powers.name: Howl of the Great Hound
powers.description: Choose to frighten enemies or empower allies with advantage on their next action.

specialRules: After Spirit Form ends, Calvin becomes tired and cannot use it again until the next session. Spirit awakening may be triggered when a friend is in serious danger, a powerful enemy appears, a major story moment occurs, or Calvin chooses loyalty over fear.

inventory.name: Extending pole hammer
inventory.charges: Equipped; extends from a 5-foot walking stick to a 10-foot war hammer on a pole

sessionNotes: Great Hound appearance / glow: Blue glow. Plot mystery: What's up with these strange dreams I have been having? Great Hound personality, favorite move, and awakening catchphrase remain unrecorded.

name: Fiona Blossom Flare
title: Protective holy knight
subtitle: Knight & Paladin of Aureth
summary: Fiona is a brave and protective knight who serves Aureth. Her holy abilities center on battlefield healing, radiant swordsmanship, and instinctively shielding others. Her golden paladin armor responds most strongly when she acts out of protectiveness.
details: Knight and paladin of Aureth, Goddess of Magic.

powers.name: Battlefield Healing
powers.description: Channels holy magic to heal or stabilize allies during battle. Exact healing dice and number of uses remain to be established.

powers.name: Brass Wings of Protection
powers.description: The brass wings connected to Fiona’s golden paladin armor awaken in moments of protection or protectiveness and can wrap around Fiona or shield up to two other people.
powers.usesRange: Self or up to 2 others; uses TBD

powers.name: Wind-Harnessed Glide
powers.description: Uses the wings to glide from high places or ride strong updrafts; cannot take off from level ground, hover, or maintain powered flight.

relationships: Bonded in holy service to Aureth, Goddess of Magic. Recognized by the dwarves through the Feast of Ancestors honor and carries a ceremonial ticket granting entry or favor.
specialRules: Golden Paladin Armor provides holy protection. Fiona’s sword can ward off undead; exact mechanical bonuses are TBD.
attackRules: Demon Banishment can return demons to the Nine Hells, but the required hit, saving throw, damage threshold, and usage limit are TBD. Undead Warding radius, duration, and save are TBD.
sessionNotes: The source notes a handwritten jewelry addition, but its details are not clear enough to confirm.

name: Golo
title: Archer, Hunter & Artifact Bearer
subtitle: Half-Giant / Half-Centaur Archer
summary: A powerful centaur archer and hunter whose dwarven alliances grant him rune magic, the magically lightweight Hammer of Earthshatter, and responsibility for a major artifact.
details: Half-Giant / Half-Centaur archer, hunter, and artifact bearer.

powers.name: Master Archer
powers.description: Uses strength, range, and practiced accuracy to strike targets with bows and magical arrows.

powers.name: Ice Arrows
powers.description: Fires magically empowered ice arrows that can damage, freeze, slow, or counter heat and fire.

powers.name: Licensed Fire Rune
powers.description: Uses dwarven-licensed fire rune power under the terms of his employment contract.

powers.name: Hammer of Earthshatter
powers.description: Instantly explodes or powders a 10-foot radius of non-living stone, including non-living spirit-conjured rock.

powers.name: Magically Lightweight Hammer
powers.description: The hammer is easy to wield regardless of normal weight and can be lent to other characters for use.

relationships: Trusted by the dwarves as artifact bearer and rune licensee. Butcher's Guild bond established through the Iceman connection.
specialRules: Earthshatter affects non-living stone and rock conjurations, but does not directly destroy living creatures. The hammer is magically lightweight and may be wielded by anyone Golo lends it to.

name: Queen Flower of Veylathar
title: Queen Regent
subtitle: Queen Regent of Veylathar
summary: Queen Flower rules Veylathar as Queen Regent, balancing personal authority, public sentiment, taxation, and council oversight. Her astral projection is conducted through the two halves of her ancestral pendant and her enchanted chalkboard map in the Castle Tower.
details: Queen Regent of Veylathar

powers.name: Royal Authority
powers.description: May raise or lower taxes, influence public sentiment, and propose use of public funds.

powers.name: Astral Projection - Seen
powers.description: Projects visibly through the linked pendant halves to the party's current location in the material realm, but cannot be heard or physically felt.

powers.name: Astral Projection - Heard
powers.description: Projects her voice through the linked pendant halves to the party's current location in the material realm, but cannot be seen or physically felt.

powers.name: Astral Projection - Felt
powers.description: Exerts physical influence through the linked pendant halves at the party's current location in the material realm, but cannot be seen or heard.

powers.name: Personal Treasury
powers.description: Receives 50 gold per week for discretionary personal spending; other tax revenue requires council approval. Tax revenue may also be rolled once per in-game month.

specialRules: Astral projection requires the two linked halves of the ancestral pendant. Queen Flower must be wearing one half, while the other half may travel with the player party. As long as both halves remain within the same material realm, the traveling half appears as a glowing point on the enchanted chalkboard map in her Castle Tower. By placing her finger on that point while wearing her half of the pendant, she can project to the party's location. Astral projection currently allows only one manifestation at a time: Seen, Heard, or Felt. A future upgrade may allow two manifestations simultaneously. Tax increases can generate unrest; tax reductions can improve public favor.
attackRules: Astral Influence - Felt hits when Queen Flower's roll exceeds the enemy's AC and deals 1d4 damage.
sessionNotes: Character sheet updated from August 2026 handwritten test photos.

name: Sertraline
title: Druidic Advisor
subtitle: Jungle Panther / Druidic Advisor
summary: A telepathic jungle panther whose practiced druidic control and tactical instincts allow her to disrupt psychic domination and command nearby vegetation with precision.
details: Jungle Panther and Druidic Advisor.

powers.name: Telepathic Communication
powers.description: Communicates directly through the minds of nearby people and entities.

powers.name: Psychic Interruption
powers.description: Telepathically screams into a target’s mind to interrupt psychic attacks, mind control, concentration, or control effects.

powers.name: Active Druidic Control
powers.description: Consciously commands vines and vegetation from half a movement away with deliberate, practiced control.

powers.name: Stealth & Jungle Mastery
powers.description: Moves quietly, tracks through natural terrain, and operates with strong tactical awareness.

powers.name: Wisp Cloak Command
powers.description: Commands a troop of Wisp Cloaks and can direct them as agents or protectors.

relationships: Bond of admiration with Garoth; respects his strength and seeks training from him.
specialRules: Two agents are tailing the former queen to determine whether she is connected to Jerry Mander or the thefts. No contact with Jerry Mander has been detected. Investigation suggests each burned Snap Match destroys a piece of reality and enlarges a growing rift rather than simply opening a portal.
sessionNotes: Character sheet updated from August 2026 handwritten photos. The recharge or time unit after the uses counts for Telepathic Communication, Psychic Interruption, and Active Druidic Control was not written on the sheet and remains unresolved.

name: Aureth — Daughter of Fate and Author of Magic
summary: Aureth emerged from the first doubt as the embodiment of possibility. She is the Old God's daughter in a metaphysical sense: formed from his own uncertainty, but possessing an identity and purpose of her own.
details: Aureth emerged from the first doubt as the embodiment of possibility. She is the Old God's daughter in a metaphysical sense: formed from his own uncertainty, but possessing an identity and purpose of her own. What Aureth Represents Possibility rather than certainty. The unexplored path. The meaningful risk of choosing without knowing the result. The idea that a future can be shaped rather than merely received. The creative space between what must happen and what might happen. Aureth's Relationship to Fate She is not simply rebellion made divine. She proves that doubt was always latent within F

name: Before the First Doubt
summary: In the oldest version of creation, the Old God of Fate existed alone. Fate was not merely a being who predicted events. Fate was the principle that events could happen only one way.
details: In the oldest version of creation, the Old God of Fate existed alone. Fate was not merely a being who predicted events. Fate was the principle that events could happen only one way. There was no uncertainty because nothing had ever departed from the intended pattern. Choice may have appeared to exist, but every choice had only one final answer. Possibility had not yet become an independent force. The Old God understood reality as a complete design rather than an unfolding story. Before doubt, the future was not unknown. It was simply waiting to arrive.

summary: The Dream Plane is a shifting borderland connected to the Ethereal Realm. It is made from sleeping minds, remembered places, fears, hopes, and futures that have not yet become real. Unlike ordinary prophecy, the Dream Plane does not show what will happen. It shows what may happen, what once almost happened, and what a person believes might happen.

name: The First Doubt
summary: At some unknowable moment, the Old God of Fate experienced the first doubt. This was not a minor hesitation. It was the first event that Fate had not fully contained within certainty.
details: At some unknowable moment, the Old God of Fate experienced the first doubt. This was not a minor hesitation. It was the first event that Fate had not fully contained within certainty. The doubt created a crack within Fate's own mind or divine nature. That crack was the first space in which more than one future could exist. The existence of doubt did not destroy Fate, but it made Fate incomplete. From that internal fracture, possibility became capable of taking form. details: The Old God of Fate is not necessarily seeking simple conquest. The restoration effort is driven by a belief that reality has become dangerously fragmented by uncertainty. name: The Origin and Nature of Magic
summary: Magic exists because Aureth discovered the spaces where fate could bend. A spell does not need to shatter destiny. It creates a temporary path through which another outcome can become real.
details: Magic exists because Aureth discovered the spaces where fate could bend. A spell does not need to shatter destiny. It creates a temporary path through which another outcome can become real. Divination explores futures that have not yet hardened into certainty. Transformation allows a creature to occupy a different possible form. name: DM Secret 2
summary: DM Direction: Aureth should not be revealed as an ordinary benevolent goddess who opposes an evil god. She represents necessary uncertainty, but uncertainty can also cause fear, loss, chaos, and painf
details: DM Direction: Aureth should not be revealed as an ordinary benevolent goddess who opposes an evil god. She represents necessary uncertainty, but uncertainty can also cause fear, loss, chaos, and painful responsibility. Her value comes from making meaningful choice possible.

name: DM Secret 3
summary: Recommended interpretation: Calvin should not be revealed as secretly more important than every other hero. His special role is practical and thematic: he can take the group into a realm none of them
details: Recommended interpretation: Calvin should not be revealed as secretly more important than every other hero. His special role is practical and thematic: he can take the group into a realm none of them could safely navigate alone, while the other heroes remain essential to surviving and understanding what they find there.

name: DM Secret 4

details: Recommended interpretation: Jerry is most compelling if he believes freedom produces disorder and that he alone is willing to impose the structure necessary to save people from themselves. His name and political methods can mirror his supernatural goal: shaping boundaries so outcomes favor his chosen design.

details: Final DM Note: The mythology should remain flexible enough to respond to the children's choices.
